write_move: Drag to move this line, or use the arrow keys
write_needs_both_yield: Makes needs both how many and of what.
write_needs_minutes: {field} takes whole hours and minutes, or nothing.
write_needs_nutrition: The Nutrition figure has to be a number, or left empty.
write_nutrition_hint: Optional. Kamosu never works it out from the lines above.
write_paste_card_title: Have the recipe as text already?
write_paste_card_body: Copy it from a message, a note or a web page. Kamosu sorts it into title, ingredients and method, and shows you what it made before anything is filled in.
write_paste_fresh: Nothing is saved until you save.
write_paste_hint: Copy the whole recipe from a message, a note or a web page. Kamosu sorts it into title, ingredients and method, and you check it before anything is filled in.
write_paste_no_title: No title in it, so type one in afterwards.
write_paste_nothing: There is nothing in that paste.
write_paste_offer: Paste it, Kamosu sorts it out
write_paste_or_yourself: or fill it in yourself below
write_paste_replaces: This replaces the {ingredients} ingredients and {steps} steps here. Nothing is saved until you save.
write_paste_start_here: Start the method at this line
write_photo_cover: or leave it, and a Cover gets drawn for you
write_photo_failed: That picture could not be kept.
write_said_fork_sent: You were sent this recipe, so your changes go into your own copy of {title}, in your Cookbook. The one you were sent stays as it arrived.
write_said_fork_theirs: This recipe is in {names}’s Cookbook, so your changes go into your own copy of {title}, in your Cookbook. {names}’s stays as it is.
write_said_fork_theirs_named: This recipe is in {cookbook}, so your changes go into your own copy of {title}, in your Cookbook. {names}’s stays as it is.
write_said_save: Saving adds a Version to your {title}, in your Cookbook.
write_saved_collapsed: Joined to your last save, not a new history entry.
write_saved_copied: Your own copy is made. You are standing in it now.
write_step_rule: A Step is a sentence and, if you like, a photograph. No timers or temperatures.
write_translation_what: This makes a new recipe in {language}, in the same family. The original is untouched.
write_will_fork: This will start your own copy
write_makes_noun: Of what: servings, a loaf, jars…
write_where_onto_said: A new Version of it, in your Cookbook.
write_where_beside_said: A second {title}. The first stays exactly as it was.
write_saved_varied: Started {name}. The first one is still there, as it was.
wrong_body: This is a mistake in Kamosu, not you. Nothing you wrote is lost. Trying again probably won't help.
you_name_changed: Done. Your Versions now say {name}. Sign in with that name from now on.
you_name_explained: The name on your Versions, and the one you sign in with.
you_name_reach_sign_in: You'll sign in with the new name. Recipe files already sent keep the old one.
you_name_reach_versions: Every Version you ever saved shows the new name, in every Kitchen.
cookbook_name_note: Named after its writer until you rename it.
cookbook_name_note_together: Named after its writers until one of you renames it.
cookbook_count_one: 1 recipe. Only this Cookbook's writers change it. Your Kitchens read and cook it.
cookbook_count: {count} recipes. Only this Cookbook's writers change them. Your Kitchens read and cook them.
cookbook_invite_said: Send this to the person. Opening it makes your recipes one Cookbook you both change. Works once.
cookbook_leave_said: You take a copy of all {count} recipes, with their history. The others keep theirs.
cookbook_leave_said_links: After that, your copies and theirs change separately. Recipes you started keep their Share Links.
cookbook_invite_title: {names} asks you to write one Cookbook together
cookbook_invite_join_said: Your {yours} recipes join their {theirs}. Either of you can then change all {total}, and your Kitchens see them.
cookbook_invite_leave_any_time: You can leave any time, with a copy of every recipe.
cookbook_invite_gone: This invite has been used or ended. Ask for a new one.
switch_on_yours: Tap another version to read it. Lines it doesn't share with yours are marked.
cookbook_invite_waiting: An invite to write it with you is waiting to be opened.
cookbook_remove_said: {name} takes a copy of all {count} recipes, with their history. You keep yours.
cookbook_invite_join_said_all: Your {yours} recipes join their {theirs}. Any of you can then change all {total}, and your Kitchens see them.
cookbook_invite_asks: {names} will be asked too. Nothing changes until everyone says yes.
cookbook_invite_waiting_on: You said yes. Waiting for {names} to say yes too.
cookbook_join_asked_said: {total} recipes in one Cookbook, which all of you can change. Nothing changes until everyone says yes.
cookbook_join_refused_leave_first: To join anyway, leave this Cookbook first. You keep a copy of every recipe. Then open the same link again.
offline_waits_write: Writing a recipe waits for the server
offline_waits_paste: Pasting a recipe waits for the server
offline_waits_pdf: Reading a PDF waits for the server
recipe_version_name_failed: The name could not be saved. Try again.
recipe_version_name_what: Shows on this version's chip at the top. The recipe and its History don't change.
story_1_say: Every recipe you cook, in one place.
story_1_said: Kamosu keeps all your recipes, and remembers how each one turned out, every time you cooked it.
story_2_say: Screenshots, bookmarks, Mum’s texts… sound familiar?
story_2_said: Recipes end up everywhere. When you want one, it’s never where you look.
story_3_say: Now they’re all in your Cookbook.
story_3_said: Add a recipe from a web link, paste it, type it in, or have an AI assistant read a screenshot. Only you can change your Cookbook.
story_4_say: Each time you cook, you write a note in the diary.
story_4_said: 3 May: “Lovely.” 14 May: “Too hot for Sam.” The recipe stays the same.
story_5_say: Next time, you use 1 chilli instead of 2.
story_5_said: You change it while cooking. The diary records what you actually cooked. The recipe still says 2.
story_6_say: It worked, so you keep the change.
story_6_said: Tap “Keep it as a new Version”. The recipe now says 1 chilli. The old Version, with 2, is still there.
story_7_say: Ever had to ask for that recipe again?
story_7_said: Sam and Inès use Kamosu too. Put your three Cookbooks in a Kitchen, and each of you can open all three.
story_8_say: Their recipes show up next to yours.
story_8_said: Sam’s lasagne, Inès’s ramen, your curry: one list, each recipe marked with whose it is. They can open and cook yours, but only you can change them.
story_9_say: Inès cooks your curry, and wants it hotter.
story_9_said: Your recipe stays yours. If Inès edits it, her changes go into a copy of her own, in her Cookbook, linked to yours.
story_10_say: And the everyday stuff is covered.
story_10_said: A shopping list that adds up the recipes you picked. A cooking screen that doesn’t go to sleep. A link to send any recipe to anyone. And your recipes stay on your phone when the wifi drops.
story_11_said: This invite creates your account and your Cookbook. Once you’re in, anyone here can invite you into their Kitchen.
story_11_said_about: Want in? Ask whoever sent you this link for an invite.
story_mum_2: 250 g red lentils, 1 onion, 2 tsp cumin. Simmer 25 min.
story_note_3: 1 chilli instead of 2. Sam had seconds.
story_offline: Every recipe in your Kitchen is on this phone.
story_offline_device: Every recipe in your Kitchen is on this device.

plus_paste_why: Kamosu sorts it into title, ingredients and method
plus_paste_no_title: No title in it, so give it one here.
plus_link_why: A web page with a recipe on it
plus_file_why: A recipe shared from another Kamosu
plus_pdf_why: A recipe printed or saved as a PDF
plus_pdf_full: Add a recipe from a PDF

share_file_failed: The file could not be saved. Try again in a moment.
drop_recipes_pdf_then: Kamosu sorts it into title, ingredients and method. You check it before the recipe is made.
drop_recipes_bundle: Drop to bring in this recipe

drop_recipes_link_then: Kamosu reads the recipe on the web page the link leads to.
drop_recipes_takes: Recipes takes a PDF, a Kamosu zip file, or a link to a web page.
drop_recipes_refused: That didn't go anywhere. Recipes takes a PDF, a Kamosu zip file, or a link to a web page.
drop_photo_recipe_then: It becomes the recipe's photograph when you save.
drop_photo_recipe_takes: A recipe's photograph has to be a picture.
drop_photo_recipe_refused: That didn't go anywhere. A recipe's photograph has to be a picture.
drop_photo_step: Drop to add it to step {number}
drop_photo_step_refused: That didn't go anywhere. A step's photograph has to be a picture.
drop_photo_cooking_refused: That didn't go anywhere. A cooking's photograph has to be a picture.
